properties.name: The governance mode is chosen, visible and changeable — it is the one asserted default that is actually acted upon
properties.statement:
Project.mode decides whether the design or the implementation is the source of truth, and reflow2 applies it by default, never asks for it, and provides no way to change it.

THE MEASURED STATE, 2026-07-28. genesis.rs takes mode OPTIONALLY — "if let Some(mode) = opts.mode" — and its own comment states the consequence: "Scaffold the Project (schema applies mode=flexible, status=active when unset)". project_mode_of falls back to "flexible" again on read. The string "mode" does not appear anywhere in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/service.rs, so there is no set_project_mode and no setter of any kind on the served surface; after genesis it is reachable only through the create_node escape hatch — the same shape as the KPP objective finding and Requirement.concern. And reflow2's OWN Project carries mode = flexible, which nobody chose.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE TEN PROPERTIES IN THE ORIGINAL SWEEP, and the difference is the whole point. Those defaults are asserted AND UNREAD — Requirement.concern sitting at core on 67 of 67 is inert, carrying no information and driving nothing. This one is asserted AND ACTED UPON: heal.rs:431 reads it, and in rigid mode HEAL only proposes and never auto-applies. So req:defaults-do-not-assert has, in this property, its first instance where the invented value changes what the system DOES. flexible is not a neutral setting either: in the vocabulary reflow2 inherited it means the architecture is NOT the source of truth, the implementation drives the architecture, and the response to drift is to update the design to match the build. That is a governance decision. reflow2 — a project whose thesis is that the design is the memory — is currently running in the mode that says the implementation drives the design, not because anyone decided so but because opts.mode was None.

THE PRIOR ART IS A MODEL, NOT A FAILURE — CORRECTED 2026-07-28, same day. This requirement was first written claiming that reflow defined development_mode, required it as the P0-to-P1 prerequisite, read it in resync_protocol and tested for it in 97, but that NO WORKFLOW STEP ANYWHERE SET IT. That claim was wrong, and the error was method rather than reasoning: the search covered workflows/*.json and did not recurse into workflows/phases/. reflow DOES elicit it, and does so better than reflow2. workflows/phases/P0_setup/phase_definition.json carries a development_mode_configuration block whose own description reads "This is where the critical development mode choice is made", and it puts a labelled question to the user — "What type of project is this?" — with two options carrying real descriptions: flexible, "Personal / Exploratory / Agile — architecture can evolve with implementation, design is a living document"; and rigid, "Enterprise / Approved / Regulated — architecture is locked after approval, implementation must conform, changes require formal approval". It then asks TWO follow-ups: if rigid, what level of drift is acceptable (none 0%, minimal 10%, or threshold-only, "threshold requirements locked, objectives flexible"); and always, "How many development/test iterations before forced architecture review?", default 3 over a range of 1 to 10. So all three governing values — mode, drift tolerance and iteration budget — were ELICITED per project rather than assumed, and the numbers that appear hardcoded elsewhere in reflow are the defaults of questions actually asked.

The correction strengthens this requirement rather than weakening it. The comparison is no longer "both systems have the same hole" but the sharper one: reflow asked the user three questions before letting the project proceed, and reflow2 asks none of them and cannot be told the answers afterwards.

THREE THINGS THIS REQUIRES, and they are separable. (1) The value is CHOSEN — genesis asks, or the mode reads as unspecified until someone says, per the rule ver:interface-spec already sets for Interface.medium: a default may record absence, never a choice. reflow's phrasing is worth reusing; it asks about the PROJECT ("what type of project is this?") rather than about a setting, which is what makes it answerable by someone who has never heard of the field. (2) The value is CHANGEABLE — a project's governance legitimately moves as it matures, exploratory to controlled, and today it cannot; brainmaker reported this from the field, half-right, since the sharper fact is that genesis does not set it at all, it defaults it. (3) The value is VISIBLE — a mode that silently changes HEAL's behaviour should be readable in the reports that say where the design stands.

What rigid should MEAN beyond heal.rs:431 stays open and parked separately on Anthony's word; this requirement is the prior question, because rigid cannot mean anything useful while the mode is unchoosable and unchangeable. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing 00a-basic_setup.json; prior-art claim corrected the same day after reviewing workflows/phases/.
